transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You multiplied speed by time, but the units don't match—what unit is the speed in, and what unit should it be to get distance in meters?
Oh, the speed is km per hour. So I need meters per second? Is it 72 divided by 3.6, so 20?
Yes, you're on the right track—convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6. What's 72 divided by 3.6?
It's 20. So 20 times 5 is 100 meters. But why do you divide by 3.6 though?
You're right—20 times 5 is 100 meters. We divide by 3.6 because 1 km/h equals 1000 meters per 3600 seconds, which simplifies to 1/3.6 m/s.
Oh right, 1000 meters in a km and 3600 seconds in an hour, so 1000 over 3600 is 1 over 3.6. So it's 100 meters. Got it, thanks.
You've got it—1000 meters in a kilometer and 3600 seconds in an hour give you 1/3.6 m/s. Great job!
